_source.title: 都市鉄道の混雑率調査結果 (Urban Railway Congestion Rate Survey)

_what_this_covers: MLIT publishes the congestion rate (混雑率) for ONE critical section per
line per direction, measured over the single busiest hour. That is the
entire extent of public segment-level loading data for the Yamanote.
* loading at any other time of day
Station boarding counts (data/ridership.csv) cannot be turned into
segment loading without an OD matrix, and no OD matrix is public. Building
a full 'load around the loop' curve would therefore mean inventing the OD
matrix and presenting the output as data. This project does not do that.
What the GUI shows instead: real station busyness from published boardings,
and the real peak congestion rate on the two sections where it is measured.

congestion_scale.100: Able to sit, or hold a hanging strap or a door-area pillar.
congestion_scale.150: Shoulders touching; many passengers crowded near the doors.
congestion_scale.180: Bodies pressed together, but a newspaper can still be read.
congestion_scale.200: Bodies pressed against each other with considerable pressure.

outer_loop.note: Congestion rate = actual passengers / train capacity over the peak hour.

inner_loop.note: MLIT identifies this as the inner loop's critical section. The rate for this direction was not captured in the source consulted; recorded as a known gap rather than filled with the outer-loop figure.

context.note: The Yamanote's 125% sits below the Tokyo average of 136%, which surprises people. Very high frequency (roughly 2.5 minute headway) spreads demand across many trains.

_note: Congestion rate maps onto the model's load_factor parameter, which is
passengers as a fraction of nominal capacity (1,724 for an 11-car E235).
A congestion rate of 125% corresponds to load_factor 1.25 and adds roughly
26 tonnes over nominal, which measurably changes acceleration.
This mapping is exact by definition -- both quantities are 'passengers
divided by rated capacity' -- so it is one of the few places in this
project where a published figure feeds the physics directly.
